title: Comparison and Logical Operators
objectives: Combine conditions with and, or, not

content.title: Comparison Operators
content.explanation: Comparisons evaluate to True or False. They work on numbers, strings (lexicographic), and other comparable types.
key_points: Chaining: 1 < x < 10 is valid and means 1 < x and x < 10

content.title: Comparison Examples
content.code:
x = 10
y = 20

print(x == y)   # False
print(x != y)   # True
print(x < y)    # True
print(x > y)    # False
print(x <= 10)  # True
print(x >= 10)  # True

# Chaining
print(0 < x < 100)  # True
print(5 < x < 15)   # True
content.explanation: Chained comparisons are evaluated as a single expression with implicit 'and'.

content.title: Logical Operators and Short-Circuit Evaluation
content.explanation: and, or, not combine boolean expressions. Python uses short-circuit evaluation: it stops evaluating as soon as the result is determined.
key_points: and: returns first falsy value, or last value if all truthy
or: returns first truthy value, or last value if all falsy
Short-circuit: x and y - if x is falsy, y is never evaluated

content.title: Logical Operator Examples
content.code:
a = 10
b = 0
c = 5

print(a and c)   # 5 (both truthy, returns last)
print(a and b)   # 0 (b is falsy, returns b)
print(a or c)    # 10 (a is truthy, returns a)
print(b or c)    # 5 (b falsy, returns c)
print(not a)     # False
print(not b)     # True
content.explanation: and/or return the actual operand value, not just True/False. This enables patterns like default = value or default_value.

content.title: Short-Circuit Prediction
content.code:
x = 0
y = 10
print(x and y / x)  # No ZeroDivisionError!
print(y or x / y)   # No ZeroDivisionError!
content.question: Why no error?
options: Short-circuit: x is 0 (falsy), so y/x never evaluated
content.correct_answer: Short-circuit: x is 0 (falsy), so y/x never evaluated
content.explanation: For 'x and y/x', since x is 0 (falsy), Python returns 0 immediately without evaluating y/x.

content.title: and vs or Return Values
content.explanation: and/or return operand values, not just booleans. Useful for defaults: name = input() or

exercises.title: Comparison Practice
exercises.description: Write comparisons to check: is x between 10 and 20 (inclusive)? Is y outside range 0-100? Are a and b equal?
exercises.starter_code:
x = 15
y = 150
a = 42
b = 42
# Write comparisons
exercises.solution:
x = 15
y = 150
a = 42
b = 42
print(10 <= x <= 20)   # True
print(y < 0 or y > 100)  # True
print(a == b)            # True
hints: Use chained comparison for range check

exercises.title: Logical Combinations
exercises.description: Given age = 25, has_license = True, write conditions: can drive (age >= 18 and has_license), is adult (age >= 18), is minor (not adult).
exercises.solution:
age = 25
has_license = True
can_drive = age >= 18 and has_license
is_adult = age >= 18
is_minor = not is_adult
print(can_drive, is_adult, is_minor)
hints: Combine with and, negate with not

exercises.title: Operator Precedence
exercises.description: Add parentheses to make each expression evaluate to True: 2 + 3 * 4 == 14, 2 + 3 * 4 == 20, not True or False == False.
exercises.starter_code:
# Add parentheses
print((2 + 3) * 4 == 20)
# Fix the others
exercises.solution:
print(2 + 3 * 4 == 14)          # True (14 == 14)
print((2 + 3) * 4 == 20)       # True (20 == 20)
print(not (True or False) == False)  # True (not True == False)
print(not True or False == False)     # True (False or False == False)
hints: * before +, not before and before or, == before not

exercises.title: Mixed Expression Evaluation
exercises.description: Evaluate step by step: 10 > 5 and 3 < 7 or False, 2 ** 3 + 1 == 9, (5 + 3) * 2 // 4.
exercises.solution:
print(10 > 5 and 3 < 7 or False)  # True
print(2 ** 3 + 1 == 9)            # True
print((5 + 3) * 2 // 4)           # 4
hints: Follow precedence: **, *,/,//,%, +,-, comparisons, not, and, or

quiz.question: What does 'a < b < c' mean in Python?
quiz.explanation: Chained comparisons are equivalent to 'and' of pairwise comparisons.

quiz.question: What is the result of: True and False or True?
quiz.explanation: and binds tighter than or. (True and False) or True = False or True = True.
